How accurate · Digital twin: one year, 495 wells

How accurate is it?

A forecast is only useful if it holds up when the answer isn't known yet. So we tested ours the honest way: pretend it is an earlier date, forecast from that point, then compare with what really happened.

How we tested

  1. Go back in time. We picked 8 dates between December 2025 and July 2026.
  2. Hide the future. At each date, the model saw only the readings up to that day.
  3. Forecast every well 1, 2, 4, 8 and 12 weeks ahead, about 3,600 forecasts per horizon.
  4. Check against reality. Measure how far off each forecast was.

Iteration 1 test design (September 2026). Later scoring, for the ML forecaster and Stage 2, forecasts from every week of the test year rather than 8 dates. Current numbers →

We also ran an automatic check that scrambles all data after each test date. The forecasts did not change at all, which proves they never peeked at the future.

The further ahead, the harder: how far off the forecasts were

Twelve weeks ahead, our forecasts were off by 1.3 m on average, against 2.8 m for assuming the level stays put: 52% less error.

Are the ranges honest?

Every forecast comes with an "80% likely" range. If that label is true, the real level should land inside the range about 8 times out of 10. It did.

1 week ahead80% heldrange about ±0.7 m
2 weeks ahead79% heldrange about ±0.7 m
4 weeks ahead81% heldrange about ±1.0 m
8 weeks ahead80% heldrange about ±1.3 m
12 weeks ahead80% heldrange about ±1.8 m

One week ahead

Over a single week the water barely moves, so even "assume nothing changes" does well. Most of the remaining error is ordinary week-to-week wobble in the readings.

The very short term: each pumping session

A separate set of models predicts what happens during and just after each pump run. They are useful for spotting a session that will pull the water unusually deep.

Level at the end of a pump run1.2 maverage error; 3.8 m if you assume no change
Level when the pump next starts1.4 maverage error; 3.7 m if you assume no change

Tested month by month from November 2025. Trained on only the last 15 days, the same models scored 1.25 m and 1.46 m: for these very short-term questions, recent data matters most.

What this shows
  • Forecasts up to 12 weeks ahead beat simple guesses, and the gap grows with time.
  • In this twin, rainfall matters: it is what separates our forecast from "the trend continues". Later twins differ (why).
  • The ranges mean what they say.
What is not proven yet
  • All of this is on a digital twin (simulated wells), not yet on years of real records.
  • We could not yet test forecasting through a monsoon: the year's only monsoon was needed to learn from.
  • Nothing beyond 12 weeks has been tested.

What we need to prove it on real wells →

Borewell Forecast is a proof of concept for forecasting groundwater levels in Bengaluru borewells. Results are labelled by where the data came from: vendor export (15 days, July 2026, in the vendor's real format but with demonstration water-level values), synthetic test system (450 simulated wells with a known answer) or digital twin (physics-based simulations of the 579 wells: one year in iteration 1, five years in later iterations and in Stage 2). No real water-level measurement has been used yet, and nothing here is yet a validated field forecast. Built by the FARII consortium.
